thread:
marta: Heads-up — intermittent east-west latency spikes across gpu-pool-east during the peak batching ramp (approx 11:52–12:05 UTC). p95 ~12ms -> p99 ~45ms, a few batch requests hit timeouts and fell back to CPU instances.

marta: sample log snippets:```
2026-03-18T11:52:12Z batch-runner[pid=4321] WARN request_id=abc123 roundtrip=120ms route=gpu-pool-east
2026-03-18T11:52:37Z batch-runner[pid=4321] WARN request_id=def456 timeout waiting for kv-cache
```

infra-bot: ALERT: e2w-latency-spike triggered (gpu-pool-east). metric: interpod.rtt.p99 = 45ms, packet_loss=0.8% over 3m. Link: https://internal.metrics/r/alerts/8891

liam: @marta can you paste `ethtool -k` and `ip link` for one of the affected nodes? also `tc -s qdisc show dev eth0` if possible.

marta: quick outputs from node gpu-east-21:```
$ ip link show eth0
3: eth0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 9000 qdisc fq_codel state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether 3a:1b:2c:3d:4e:5f brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
$ ethtool -k eth0
Features for eth0:
rx-checksumming: on
scatter-gather: on
tcp-segmentation-offload: on
generic-segmentation-offload: on
generic-receive-offload: on
```

marta: note: some nodes in the pool show mtu=1500 (legacy hosts) — not all 9000. could be MTU mismatch + offloads triggering fragmentation at the host/ToR.

anya: we rolled an mlx5 driver + RDMA tuning two nights ago for RoCE tests in that fleet. there was a sysctl change: `net.core.rps_sock_flow_entries` bumped to 32768 and `dev.mlx5_core.rq_moderation_us=9` on some nodes. might be related.

sanjay: seeing qdisc drop counters climb around the same windows. sample `tc` output from gpu-east-21:```
qdisc fq_codel 0: dev eth0 root refcnt 2 limit 10240p flows 1024 quantum 1514 target 5.0ms
  backlog 0b 0p requeues 0
  memory limit 8Mb
  packets 1248196 bytes 1.0G dropped 568 overrun 0
```

liam: hypothesis: offloading + MTU mismatch causing segmentation and intermittent RX queue overload -> fq_codel starts dropping/queuing leading to higher tail latency for east-west RPCs. quick mitigation: disable GRO/GSO/TSO on a canary host and see if latency normalizes. command: `sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off`

marta: did the canary on gpu-east-21 at 12:14. after toggling offloads p99 dropped to ~8ms and batch timeouts stopped. no more immediate packet_loss alerts.

liam: nice. so plan: 1) roll `ethtool -K` change across the affected pool via fleet job for the duration of the hot path; 2) revert RDMA mlx5 tunables we added unless we can test safe set; 3) add alert on qdisc dropped > 50/min and interpod.rtt.p99 > 20ms for gpu-pools.

sanjay: I'll prepare the fleet job and a scoped kernel/driver audit. also add a quick script to check MTU consistency across the pool: `for n in $(nodes); do ssh $n ip link | grep -E "mtu"; done` and fail the job if any mtu != 9000.

noah: what's the customer/cost impact? how many batches fell back to CPU and what's the rough extra cost?

marta: rough numbers: ~1200 batch requests fell back over the 13m window, ~0.3M extra CPU tokens billed (ballpark). ops cost estimate ~ $180 extra for that window. will add exact numbers to the incident doc.

anya: follow-ups: 1) revert risky mlx5 tuning unless validated; 2) add MTU drift detection to bootstrap checks; 3) add automated preflight that fails driver/rdma tunable changes if fleet heterogeneity exists; 4) update runbook for e2w latency incidents.

liam: also add a short-term SLO guard: if interpod.rtt.p99 > 25ms for >3m, auto-schedule a reduce-batch-size fallback rather than immediate retries — reduces pressure during ramps. ops-team to review.

marta: I'm going to roll the ethtool change to the rest of gpu-pool-east now (staggered). will post progress updates.

marta: update 12:52 UTC: rolled to 10/14 nodes, p99 stable across those. continuing.

infra-bot: RUNBOOK: Created incident task: INC-2026-0457, link: https://internal.incidents/INC-2026-0457

noah: thanks — please add cost notes to the incident and tag finance if we need billing adjustments.

liam: good catch, @marta and @sanjay. once the immediate mitigations finish we'll schedule a root-cause postmortem and mark whether driver rollback is needed.

marta: ack. I'll file the postmortem draft and assign owners for the 3 follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
